title: The monomial numerical criterion for Hilbert stability
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], let $r\geq2$, let $E$ be an $r$-dimensional $k$-vector space, and let $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(E^\vee)$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-scheme] of admissible coordinate Hilbert polynomial $P$ [def-sfb-projective-coordinate-hilbert-polynomial]. Write $L=\mathcal O_X(1)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist], and take any integer $m\geq M(P,r)$ for the Hilbert embedding in [lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization]. For an ordered basis $b=(b_0,\ldots,b_{r-1})$ of $E$ and rational weights $u=(u_0,\ldots,u_{r-1})$, give a degree-$m$ monomial $\prod_i b_i^{\alpha_i}$ weight $\sum_i\alpha_i u_i$. Define $W_{b,u}(m)$ to be the minimum of the sums of weights over all sets of degree-$m$ monomials whose restrictions form a $k$-basis of $H^0(X,L^{\otimes m})$ [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]; these sets exist by the surjectivity in the Hilbert embedding. Then the $m$th Hilbert point is stable for $\operatorname{SL}(E)$ with its Hilbert determinant line $\Lambda_m$, in the geometric sense of [lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization], if and only if for every ordered basis $b$ and every nonconstant rational tuple $u$ one has
$$W_{b,u}(m)<\frac{\sum_i u_i}{r}\,mP(m).$$
The equivalence holds in every characteristic, with no smoothness, reducedness or dimension assumption on $X$. Constant tuples are excluded from this strict criterion.

proof.text: Put $q=P(m)$, $S=\operatorname{Sym}^mE$, $Q=H^0(X,L^{\otimes m})$ and $D=\bigwedge^q S$. By [lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization], restriction $\pi:S\twoheadrightarrow Q$ is surjective, $\dim Q=q$, and the Hilbert scheme has an SL-equivariant Pluecker closed immersion with hyperplane line $\Lambda_m=\det Q$. Its quotient Pluecker point is $\bigwedge^q\pi:D\twoheadrightarrow\det Q$. Equivalently, after choosing a nonzero trivialization of $\det Q$, it is the line spanned by a nonzero functional $\ell\in D^*$; the lines-projective hyperplane line is precisely the quotient determinant line. Apply [lem-sfb-hilbert-mumford-projective-representation] to this Hilbert scheme, its closed immersion into $\mathbf P_{\mathrm{lines}}(D^*)$, and the induced SL representation on $D^*$. The embedding theorem gives exactly the geometric stability convention required by that criterion. No smoothness or reducedness is required by either input.

proof.text: For any homomorphism $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to\operatorname{SL}(E)$, [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] gives a basis $b_i$ of $E$ with integral weights $a_i$. In this basis its determinant character is $t^{\sum_i a_i}$. Since it is identically one as a Laurent polynomial, $\sum_i a_i=0$ as an integer, also in positive characteristic. The subgroup is nontrivial exactly when some $a_i\ne0$. Conversely every ordered basis and nonzero integral tuple of sum zero defines such a nontrivial subgroup by $b_i\mapsto t^{a_i}b_i$ over every $k$-algebra. Thus testing all nontrivial subgroups is equivalent to testing all these weighted bases.

proof.text: Fix such $(b,a)$. The degree-$m$ monomials form the usual basis of $S$; their weights are $\alpha\cdot a$. A wedge indexed by a $q$-element monomial set $I$ has weight $s_I=\sum_{\alpha\in I}\alpha\cdot a$. Its image under $\bigwedge^q\pi$ is the determinant of the images of those monomials. Hence the coordinate $\ell_I$ is nonzero exactly when their restrictions form a basis of $Q$. Surjectivity ensures at least one such $I$. Under the dual action of $\lambda^{-1}$ on $D^*$, the dual wedge basis has weights $s_I$: dualization and inversion each negate the weight. Therefore $\nu_{\lambda^{-1}}([\ell])=\min_{\ell_I\ne0}s_I=W_{b,a}(m)$. Inversion permutes nontrivial one-parameter subgroups, so step 1 gives stability exactly when $W_{b,a}(m)<0$ for every basis and nonzero integral sum-zero tuple. When $q=0$, use $\bigwedge^0S=k$ and the empty set: its coordinate is 1 and its weight 0. Thus this case fails the strict criterion, as it should.

proof.text:
For a nonconstant rational tuple $u$ put $\bar u=(\sum_i u_i)/r$. Choose a positive integer $c$ clearing the denominators of all $u_i-\bar u$ and set $a_i=c(u_i-\bar u)$. Then $a$ is a nonzero integral tuple of sum zero. Every degree-$m$ monomial of $u$-weight $v$ has $a$-weight $c(v-m\bar u)$. Every monomial basis has $q$ elements, so taking the minimum over the same finite nonempty collection gives
$$W_{b,a}(m)=c\bigl(W_{b,u}(m)-mP(m)\bar u\bigr).$$
Since $c>0$, negativity in step 3 is exactly the required inequality. Conversely the stated rational test includes every nonzero integral sum-zero tuple. For a constant tuple $u_i=d$, all basis sums equal $dmP(m)$, so strict inequality is impossible; excluding it is exactly excluding the trivial subgroup. The calculation uses integer characters and determinants only, and is valid in every characteristic.
